findings.issue_text: [BUG] The new `delete "members"` and `put "members"` routes are declared inside `resources :groups` (outside the `collection do ... end` block), so they are scoped to `/admin/groups/:id/members` (or at best `/admin/groups/members`), and in neither case does the request carry a `group_id` param, but Admin::GroupsController#add_members and #remove_member both call `params.require(:group_id)`, which raises ActionController::ParameterMissing. Every add-member/remove-member request issued by the new admin UI (which PUTs/DELETEs to `/admin/groups/<id>/members.json`) fails with a 500/400 ParameterMissing instead of modifying the group; the feature is unreachable end-to-end.

[BUG] The `remove_member` specs issue `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` while the route maps `remove_member` to the DELETE verb (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`), so the PUT requests do not match the route. Both `.remove_member` examples (including the automatic-group 422 case and the successful-removal case) hit no matching route and fail (404/routing error), so the spec suite does not pass as written.

[ADVISORY] `remove_member` uses `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `group.save`, which deletes the join row without executing GroupUser callbacks and does not recompute `group.user_count`. After a successful removal through this endpoint the group's denormalized `user_count` (displayed as `({{user_count}})` in the new admin template and used for pagination via `meta.total`) is stale until something else refreshes it, so the member pagination shows a wrong total and a phantom page.

[BUG] totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which reports 2 pages when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members at limit 50), so showingLast never becomes true and the next action stays enabled on the last page. An admin clicking 'next' on the final page of a full-size group sets offset = user_count and fetches an empty member list, wiping the visible member rows until they click 'previous'; the off-by-one also makes the page counter display a phantom empty page.

[BUG] The '.remove_member' happy-path test issues xhr :put, :remove_member, but the route is delete "members" => "groups#remove_member", so the PUT is routed to add_members with usernames nil and params.require(:usernames) raises before remove_member ever runs. The test fails (ActionController::ParameterMissing / 400 response instead of success), and if it were passing it would be passing for the wrong action — the actual remove_member happy path is never exercised.

[BUG] The members endpoint passes params[:offset].to_i straight into the SQL offset clause without clamping, so offset=-1 produces a negative OFFSET that PostgreSQL rejects. A request to /groups/:name/members.json?offset=-1 raises ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid and returns a 500 instead of a 4xx, breaking any caller that paginates backwards past zero.

[ADVISORY] add_members silently skips usernames that don't resolve to a user, and the diff deleted the old specs ('succeeds silently when adding non-existent users') without a replacement covering or documenting that behavior for the new endpoint. An admin who typos a username sees a success response and the member never appears; without an acceptance test this silent-drop behavior can change without notice.

[ADVISORY] remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), which is a silent no-op when user_id is not a member or does not exist, and no test covers that case. Stale UI state (member already removed in another tab) yields a 200 'success' with nothing deleted; the missing edge-case acceptance criterion means regressions here go undetected.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten members action (new pagination shape, meta envelope, serialize_data path) has no controller spec in the diff — the only groups_controller spec changes are for Admin::GroupsController. A regression in the new total/limit/offset envelope or the guardian visibility check on this public endpoint would ship undetected.

[ADVISORY] The GET /admin/groups/:id/users route is removed with no replacement or deprecation, and the admin client now reads members from the public /groups/:name/members.json endpoint guarded by guardian.ensure_can_see!. Any out-of-tree consumer of the old admin members endpoint gets a routing 404 with no migration note, and admin member listing now depends on the group's public visibility semantics rather than admin authorization.

[ADVISORY] The admin-group-selector component template was reduced to a bare <input type="text"> with no binding to any property. Whatever screen renders this component now shows a dead text field that writes nowhere — an incompletely-migrated path shipped in the same diff.

[ADVISORY] addMembers never clears the usernames selector (acknowledged by the in-code TODO), so the input retains the just-added usernames. An admin who clicks 'Add' twice re-submits the same usernames, and the stale list is confusing on the next add; the TODO means the acceptance criterion 'input clears after add' is knowingly unmet.

[ADVISORY] The new .create and .update contexts only cover happy paths; there is no test for the validation-failure branch (render_json_error) in create or for alias_level handling in update, both of which are new/rewritten code paths. A regression returning a 500 instead of the 422 json error body, or silently dropping alias_level updates, would not be caught by the suite.

[BUG] addMembers silently succeeds when some or all submitted usernames do not match any user, returning success_json with nothing added and no indication of which names were skipped. An admin typos 'johm' instead of 'john', gets a green success response, the member list reloads unchanged, and the admin has no way to know the add failed — membership drifts silently.

[BUG] The automatic-group protection test for remove_member issues xhr :put but the route is registered as DELETE, so the request does not match the route under test. The spec never exercises the can_not_modify_automatic guard for remove_member; it passes/fails on routing behavior, leaving the 422 path for member removal untested.

[BUG] The GET /admin/groups/users endpoint is deleted from the admin namespace with no replacement registered in this diff, breaking any existing client or integration still calling it. Out-of-tree consumers (API scripts, plugins) that listed admin group users via GET /admin/groups/users now get a 404 with no deprecation path.

[BUG] update and create drop the legacy params[:group] payload shape (and the PATCH incremental-changes contract entirely) with no back-compat or versioning, silently changing the admin API surface. Existing API consumers posting {group: {name: ..., usernames: ...}} now get a group created with a blank name or a 500 (params[:group][:name] on nil), and the PATCH /admin/groups/:id with changes:{add/delete} contract disappears entirely — callers migrate to silent no-ops or errors.

[ADVISORY] The form-horizontal styling block is moved from the customize area scope to a combined '.groups, .badges' selector, restyling the badges admin screens with no badge-related change anywhere else in this diff. Badge admin screens get wider inputs and bolder labels as an untracked side effect; if the badge team never asked for this, the visual change ships unreviewed and untraceable to any requirement.

[BUG] create no longer accepts usernames, and the admin template hides the member editor until the group has an id, so creating a group pre-populated with members is no longer possible anywhere in the product. Admins who previously created a group with its founding membership in one step must now do a two-step create-then-add; this capability loss is not stated by the PR intent 'proper handling of group memberships' and constitutes silent feature removal.

[ADVISORY] The 'TODO: fix the root cause ... more than 200 groups it will truncate' limitation is deleted rather than fixed, so the truncation root cause referenced by the removed comment is now unowned. Whatever bug caused truncation above 200 members remains in the codebase with its only documentation removed; the next person hitting it has no pointer to the root cause.

[ADVISORY] remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) then group.save, bypassing membership callbacks and making the group.save call dead weight on the happy path. Any denormalized state maintained in GroupUser callbacks or Group save hooks (e.g. user_count recalibration) is skipped, and the trailing group.save implies validation runs on removal when it does not — future maintainers will assume removal is validated and callback-driven when it is neither.

[BUG] Pagination math is off by one: totalPages = Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 yields 3 pages for 100 users at limit 50, and next() clamps offset to Math.min(offset+limit, user_count) (e.g. 101 for user_count=101), which requests a page with zero members. For any group whose member count is an exact multiple of the limit, showingLast never becomes true and the admin can page into an empty last page; for non-multiples, the clamp lands past the last page start so the final page renders an empty member list while displaying currentPage/totalPages as valid.

[BUG] add_members splits the usernames string and issues one User.find_by_username query per username inside the loop (N+1), with no batched WHERE username IN (...) lookup. Adding a large batch of members issues N sequential user lookups plus N group.add association writes instead of a batched load and one save; on an admin action over a big paste this scales linearly per-user at DB roundtrip cost.

[BUG] Usernames are split on "," without stripping whitespace or reporting unknown users, so 'bob, fred' looks up ' fred' which matches nothing, and every miss is silently dropped while the action still renders success_json. An admin pasting a comma-separated list with spaces gets a green success response with some or all members silently not added; the client then reloads a member list that doesn't include the names the admin just typed, with no error to explain why.

[BUG] The PUT /admin/groups/:id contract silently changed from the nested {group: {name, alias_level, visible, usernames}} envelope to flat top-level params, and PATCH with changes:{add/delete} plus GET /admin/groups/users were removed outright, with no versioning. Existing API consumers and scripts that PUT group[usernames] or PATCH changes get their payload fields silently ignored (usernames now dropped on update entirely — membership edits vanish), and callers of the removed routes get 404s; nothing in the diff notifies or versions these breaks.

[BUG] After removeMember on the last member of a page, findMembers clamps offset against the stale user_count (set from the previous fetch), fetches a page past the new end, and the stale offset is then persisted, leaving the UI stuck on an empty page. Removing the final member of the last page shows an empty member list with pagination controls reading a bogus currentPage/totalPages; the admin must click previous to recover, and the meta.total/user_count the next() clamp relies on was stale at request time.

[ADVISORY] limit is taken from params with no upper bound ((params[:limit] || 50).to_i), so a caller can request limit=1000000 and materialize the entire membership in one render. The public /groups/:name/members endpoint loses the previous automatic-group cap; a single request can serialize every member row, which gets bitten on large groups (memory + response size) and is trivially triggered by any visitor.

[ADVISORY] The admin-group-selector component is stripped to a bare <input type="text"> with no binding, action, or data source — a ships-inert control. Any page that still renders {{admin-group-selector}} shows a dead text field that neither autocompletes nor persists anything; whoever relies on it for group selection silently gets no behavior.

[ADVISORY] The members list template switched from iterating model to iterating members with no members property defined on the group-members controller in this diff — the value only resolves by proxying through the group model's members key set asynchronously by findMembers. The rendering depends on an implicit ObjectController proxy chain to a property that is null until the fire-and-forget findMembers() promise resolves; until then the table renders nothing with no loading state, and any refactor that drops ObjectController breaks this binding silently.

[ADVISORY] remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) and then group.save, with no verification that the user is a member or even exists, and the trailing save persists an otherwise unchanged group. Removing a non-member returns success_json (no idempotency signal distinguishing 'removed' from 'was never there'), and the redundant group.save re-runs validations on an untouched record, turning an unrelated validation failure into a 422 for a deletion that already succeeded.

[BUG] create() drops the alias_level parameter that the client's group.create() asJSON() payload still sends, so newly created groups silently lose the alias level selected in the admin UI. An admin picks an alias level when creating a group; the POST succeeds but the field is never assigned, so the group is created with the default alias level and the UI shows a different value than what was saved.

[BUG] add_members splits usernames on ',' without stripping whitespace, so 'bob, bill' looks up the user ' bill' and silently adds nothing for that entry. Admins pasting a comma-separated list with spaces get a 200 success response while some members are never added, with no error indicating which usernames failed.

[BUG] members passes params[:offset].to_i straight into the SQL offset without clamping, so a negative offset (e.g. offset=-1) generates invalid SQL and a 500 on the public /groups/:name/members endpoint. Any client (including anonymous ones, subject to visibility) sending a negative offset triggers an ActiveRecord/Postgres error instead of a 4xx, producing error noise and a 500 response.

[BUG] The GET /admin/groups/users route is deleted and the PATCH-style incremental membership update (update_patch with changes[:add]/[:delete]) is removed in the same diff, breaking the previously supported admin group API surface without deprecation. Out-of-tree consumers (scripts, API integrations, plugins) using GET /admin/groups/users or PATCH /admin/groups/:id with changes silently get 404s/routing failures after upgrade — an objective change (redesign of membership API) with no migration path or acceptance call-out.

[BUG] create() no longer accepts or sends usernames, so the long-standing ability to add initial members at group-creation time is silently removed from the admin flow. Previously an admin could create a group and seed its membership in one step (createWithUsernames); now they must create the group, wait for it to persist, then add members separately — a user-facing workflow regression introduced by iteration without explicit acceptance of the capability removal.

[ADVISORY] addMembers leaves the 'TODO: should clear the input' unresolved, so the user-selector retains the just-added usernames. After clicking Add, the usernames remain in the input; clicking Add again re-submits the same list (harmlessly re-adding duplicates but confusingly showing a stale pending set), and the admin must manually clear the field each time.

[ADVISORY] addMembers gives no feedback for usernames that don't resolve to a user — the server silently skips unknown usernames and the promise resolves with success_json. An admin who typo's a username sees success and a refreshed member list that lacks the intended user, with no indication the add partially failed; the old spec explicitly documented and accepted this silent behavior, so the new dedicated endpoint carried the gap forward rather than fixing it.

[ADVISORY] findMembers clamps offset against the possibly stale local user_count, so after member removals on later pages the client can request an offset within a shrunken range but the clamp uses the pre-refresh total. After removing members the refreshed count is fetched only via the response meta; in the window before refresh, next/previous navigation can compute offsets from a user_count that no longer matches the server, showing an empty page until the meta correction kicks in on the following fetch.

[ADVISORY] The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' test issues xhr :put against the remove_member action, which is routed as DELETE. The test exercises the wrong verb; it passes only by luck of routing/error behavior and would not catch a regression where the DELETE path loses the automatic-group guard.

[ADVISORY] remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) then group.save, using the association delete as the real mutation and wrapping it in a save that cannot meaningfully fail — validation-less dead control flow. The save/save-failure branch is dead code that implies validation exists where none does; if group.users.delete returns 0 (user not a member) the endpoint still renders success, so clients cannot distinguish 'removed' from 'was never a member'.

[ADVISORY] remove_member uses `group.users.delete(user_id)`, which deletes the join row directly and bypasses the Group membership callbacks (user_count maintenance, automatic-group refresh hooks) that Group#remove goes through. After removing a member the group's cached user_count is stale until refresh_automatic_groups/reload; any logic keyed on user_count (visibility checks, 'groups.visible' behavior, admin UI pagination totals) reports a member count that includes the removed user, and any future callback added to Group#remove (e.g. primary-group downgrade) silently never fires for this path.

[ADVISORY] add_members calls `usernames.split(",")` on `params.require(:usernames)` without asserting it is a String, so a JSON request body sending usernames as an array (the natural shape for a list of usernames) raises NoMethodError on Array#split. An admin (or an API client following the obvious JSON convention) POSTing/PUTting {usernames: ["alice","bob"]} gets a 500 instead of a 4xx; the member-add path is unusable for the JSON content-type even though the route accepts it.

[ADVISORY] The members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no cap (`(params[:limit] || 50).to_i`), so limit=-1 or an arbitrarily large value is passed straight to `.limit()`. A client can force a negative limit (which ActiveRecord treats as no limit) or a huge limit to dump the full member roster of any visible group in one request, defeating the pagination the change introduces; combined with the offset param this enables cheap bulk enumeration of members for all groups.

[BUG] The '.update ignore name change on automatic group' test hardcodes id: 1 and Group.find(1), asserting behavior against whatever group happens to have id 1 in the test database rather than a group the test creates. The test's validity depends on Discourse's seeded automatic groups keeping id 1; if fixtures/seed order changes so that group 1 is not automatic, the assertion group.name.should_not == 'WAT' silently passes for the wrong reason (name is just never set because params[:name] handling changed), and a RecordNotFound from Group.find(1) fails the suite for a reason unrelated to the behavior under test. It also never verifies that a non-automatic group CAN be renamed, so the new `group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic` branch's positive path has zero coverage in this diff.

[BUG] The '.add_members cannot add members to automatic groups' test hardcodes group_id: 1 without creating any group, relying on the assumption that group id 1 is automatic. If the test database's group with id 1 is not automatic (e.g. after fixture/seed changes or when another spec deletes/recreates groups), the request succeeds with 200 and the assertion response.status.should == 422 fails — or worse, passes vacuously through a different error path. The same applies to the remove_member automatic test at lines 126-129, which additionally issues a PUT (xhr :put, :remove_member) even though the route/action semantics are DELETE, so the test no longer matches the HTTP verb the client and router actually use.

[ADVISORY] The new add_members endpoint silently skips nonexistent usernames (User.find_by_username returns nil and nothing is added), and this diff deleted the old patch-based tests that pinned that silent-skip behavior without replacing them. A future change that makes add_members raise or 404 on an unknown username (or worse, adds a user by a different lookup) breaks user-facing behavior with no test failing; the previous suite explicitly covered 'succeeds silently when adding non-existent users' and that guarantee is now unverified.

[ADVISORY] The public GroupsController#members action's new response contract (members + meta{total,limit,offset} envelope) and its pagination clamping have no test changes anywhere in this diff. The client model group.js now depends on result.meta.total/limit/offset to compute currentPage/totalPages (findMembers sets user_count from result.meta.total); a serializer or key regression in this new envelope produces NaN page numbers and broken pagination in the admin UI with no failing spec, and the old spec (if any) asserting the previous flat serialized array shape is now stale.

[ADVISORY] The 'is able to remove a member' test never asserts the negative/edge paths of the rewritten remove_member action (non-member user_id, removing the last owner semantics, or that group.save's failure branch renders 422). The controller code `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by an unconditional group.save is new logic whose only covered path is the happy path; a regression such as delete raising on an unknown id (ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound on some association setups) or the save-error branch rendering errors would ship unnoticed.

[BUG] add_members silently skips usernames that don't resolve to a user and still renders success_json, so the client believes all requested members were added. An admin adds 'alice,bob' where 'bob' doesn't exist; the server adds only alice, returns 200 success, and the UI shows no indication that bob was dropped — the operation is silently partial with no error result or log.

[BUG] remove_member silently no-ops (and returns success) when user_id is not a member of the group, and group.save on an untouched record can never fail so the 422 branch is dead. A stale UI or double-invocation sends a user_id that was already removed; the endpoint returns success, the client reloads and shows the member still present or the removal 'succeed' with nothing done — no error distinguishes a real removal from a no-op.

[BUG] next/previous set model offset before findMembers resolves, and neither guards against concurrent in-flight requests, so failures leave the pager advanced past unloaded data and rapid clicks issue overlapping requests whose out-of-order responses overwrite newer state. If the members request fails (or two clicks race), the controller's offset points at a page whose members were never fetched; the pager shows page N+1 with stale/empty member list and no error is surfaced, and last-response-wins can desync offset from displayed members.

[BUG] findMembers attaches no rejection handler to the Discourse.ajax promise, and both callers (routes' setupController and the pager actions) invoke it fire-and-forget without returning/propagating it, so any server failure is swallowed. When /groups/:name/members.json returns an error, the user sees an empty member list (or the previous page's stale list after next/previous) with no error message; the rejected promise is unhandled and the failure is invisible.

[BUG] removeMember and addMembers attach only a .then that reloads the member list, with no .catch; a 422 (e.g. can_not_modify_automatic) or network failure leaves the UI showing the pre-operation member list with no feedback. An admin clicks remove/add on a group whose mutation is rejected; bootbox confirm closed, no error rendered, list unchanged — the user-facing operation fails invisibly.

[BUG] the members endpoint applies no upper bound to the client-supplied limit param (limit = params[:limit].to_i with no max), so a request with limit=1000000 loads and serializes the entire member table. Any visitor who can see the group can request an arbitrarily large limit, forcing a full-table query and an unbounded serialized JSON payload on the request path — memory/latency exhaustion with no cap.

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1, which reports one page too many when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, and showingLast (currentPage == totalPages) therefore leaves next enabled on a final empty page. A group with exactly 50 members at limit 50 shows '1/2'; clicking next clamps offset to user_count=50, findMembers returns an empty members array, and the admin is left staring at a blank member page reached through a control that should have been disabled.

[ADVISORY] the admin-group-selector component template was stripped to a bare <input type="text">, discarding whatever bound value/behavior it previously rendered, leaving a dead input with no wiring. Any admin surface still rendering this component gets a text box that does nothing — a silently inert element that misleads whoever next touches group selection.

[ADVISORY] setupController fires model.findMembers() without returning the promise, so the route transition completes before members load and any load failure occurs after navigation with no retry or error surface at the route level. The admin lands on the group page with an empty members section while the request is in flight; a failed request never blocks or reports — contrast with the removed afterModel which at least chained the promise.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `remove_member` uses `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `group.save`, which deletes the join row without executing GroupUser callbacks and does not recompute `group.user_count`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The members endpoint passes params[:offset].to_i straight into the SQL offset clause without clamping, so offset=-1 produces a negative OFFSET that PostgreSQL rejects. adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new code sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then unconditionally calls `.offset(offset)` (see `members = group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`). There is no clamping to `>= 0`, so a request like `?offset=-1` will pass a negative offset into ActiveRecord/PostgreSQL, which can raise an error and produce a 500. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) then group.save, bypassing membership callbacks and making the group.save call dead weight on the happy path. Any denormalized state maintained in GroupUser callbacks or Group save hooks (e.g. user_count recalibration) is skipped, and the trailing group.save implies validation runs on removal when it does not — future maintainers will assume removal is validated and callback-driven when it is neither.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `group.save` (and using `group.save`’s result to decide success vs error). The association deletion is already persisted when `delete` runs, so the subsequent `group.save` does not actually drive the removal and can be misleading (and could even report failure due to unrelated group validations despite the member having been removed). However, the finding’s stronger claim about “bypassing membership callbacks” / “denormalized state maintained in GroupUser callbacks” cannot be verified from this diff because the association type and any callbacks/counter caches are not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Pagination math is off by one: totalPages = Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 yields 3 pages for 100 users at limit 50, and next() clamps offset to Math.min(offset+limit, user_count) (e.g. 101 for user_count=101), which requests a page with zero members. For any group whose member count is an exact multiple of the limit, showingLast never becomes true and the admin can page into an empty last page; for non-multiples, the clamp lands past the last page start so the final page renders an empty member list while displaying currentPage/totalPages as valid.

[BUG] add_members splits the usernames string and issues one User.find_by_username query per username inside the loop (N+1), with no batched WHERE username IN (...) lookup. Adding a large batch of members issues N sequential user lookups plus N group.add association writes instead of a batched load and one save; on an admin action over a big paste this scales linearly per-user at DB roundtrip cost.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff shows `usernames.split(",").each` with `User.find_by_username(username)` inside the loop and `group.add(user)` per user before a final `group.save`. This is a linear per-username pattern (potential N user lookups plus per-user association writes) rather than a batched `WHERE username IN (...)` load and bulk association update. It’s a real performance/scalability concern for large pastes, but not a functional correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Usernames are split on "," without stripping whitespace or reporting unknown users, so 'bob, fred' looks up ' fred' which matches nothing, and every miss is silently dropped while the action still renders success_json. An admin pasting a comma-separated list with spaces gets a green success response with some or all members silently not added; the client then reloads a member list that doesn't include the names the admin just typed, with no error to explain why.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and then `User.find_by_username(username)` without trimming whitespace. So an input like `"bob, fred"` will look up `" fred"` and fail. It also silently ignores any username that can’t be found (no error/feedback) and still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, which can mislead admins into thinking all members were added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The PUT /admin/groups/:id contract silently changed from the nested {group: {name, alias_level, visible, usernames}} envelope to flat top-level params, and PATCH with changes:{add/delete} plus GET /admin/groups/users were removed outright, with no versioning. Existing API consumers and scripts that PUT group[usernames] or PATCH changes get their payload fields silently ignored (usernames now dropped on update entirely — membership edits vanish), and callers of the removed routes get 404s; nothing in the diff notifies or versions these breaks.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a breaking contract change for the admin groups endpoints: Admin::GroupsController#create and #update switched from nested params[:group] (old code referenced params[:group][:name], payload = params[:group], and supported PATCH via update_patch(changes:{add/delete})) to flat top-level params (params[:name], params[:visible], params[:alias_level]) and removed PATCH handling entirely. It also drops usernames processing on update (no params[:usernames] in #update) and replaces membership changes with new routes/actions (routes.rb removes `get "users"` and adds `put "members"`/`delete "members"` mapped to add_members/remove_member). This will break existing clients that still send the previous nested envelope or use PATCH/old routes, but it’s a compatibility/API-evolution concern rather than a provable functional defect within the new implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] After removeMember on the last member of a page, findMembers clamps offset against the stale user_count (set from the previous fetch), fetches a page past the new end, and the stale offset is then persisted, leaving the UI stuck on an empty page. Removing the final member of the last page shows an empty member list with pagination controls reading a bogus currentPage/totalPages; the admin must click previous to recover, and the meta.total/user_count the next() clamp relies on was stale at request time.

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group.findMembers`, the request `offset` is clamped using the *current* `user_count` on the model: `offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0));` (group.js). After `removeMember`, the code calls `self.findMembers()` without first adjusting `user_count`/`offset` (group.js `removeMember`). If you remove the only member on the last page (e.g., total=51, limit=50, offset=50), `user_count` is still 51 when `findMembers` computes `offset`, so it requests offset=50. The server now reports `meta.total=50` and returns an empty page for `limit(50).offset(50)` (groups_controller.rb), and the client then persists `offset` from `result.meta.offset` (still 50) and sets `user_count` to 50, yielding an empty `members` list while `currentPage/totalPages` still computes as 2/2 (admin-group.js.es6). This matches the described stuck-on-empty-page behavior until the admin clicks `previous`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] limit is taken from params with no upper bound ((params[:limit] || 50).to_i), so a caller can request limit=1000000 and materialize the entire membership in one render. The public /groups/:name/members endpoint loses the previous automatic-group cap; a single request can serialize every member row, which gets bitten on large groups (memory + response size) and is trivially triggered by any visitor.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` is used directly with `group.users...limit(limit)` and there is no maximum enforced, so a client can request an arbitrarily large `limit` and force serialization of a very large members list in one response (`render json: { members: serialize_data(members, ...) }`). The finding’s phrasing about “losing the previous automatic-group cap” is somewhat off (there was no true cap before either), but the diff still contains the unbounded-limit DoS/perf defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The admin-group-selector component is stripped to a bare <input type="text"> with no binding, action, or data source — a ships-inert control. Any page that still renders {{admin-group-selector}} shows a dead text field that neither autocompletes nor persists anything; whoever relies on it for group selection silently gets no behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show the admin-group-selector component being “stripped” of bindings/behavior; the only change in `admin-group-selector.hbs` is removal of surrounding blank lines, leaving the same `<input type="text">` that was already there before. No new removal of actions/data sources is evidenced by this PR diff, nor does the diff show any pages relying on `{{admin-group-selector}}` being impacted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The members list template switched from iterating model to iterating members with no members property defined on the group-members controller in this diff — the value only resolves by proxying through the group model's members key set asynchronously by findMembers. The rendering depends on an implicit ObjectController proxy chain to a property that is null until the fire-and-forget findMembers() promise resolves; until then the table renders nothing with no loading state, and any refactor that drops ObjectController breaks this binding silently.

[ADVISORY] remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) and then group.save, with no verification that the user is a member or even exists, and the trailing save persists an otherwise unchanged group. Removing a non-member returns success_json (no idempotency signal distinguishing 'removed' from 'was never there'), and the redundant group.save re-runs validations on an untouched record, turning an unrelated validation failure into a 422 for a deletion that already succeeded.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `if group.save ... else ...` (new method around lines `def remove_member`). The association `delete` already performs the join-table deletion immediately; the subsequent `group.save` is redundant and can cause the endpoint to return a 422 based on unrelated group validations/callbacks even though the membership deletion already happened. However, the finding’s claim that this is a definite defect (and that lack of member/existence checks is wrong) isn’t strictly verifiable from the diff alone—returning success when deleting a non-member can be acceptable idempotent behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] create() drops the alias_level parameter that the client's group.create() asJSON() payload still sends, so newly created groups silently lose the alias level selected in the admin UI.
